posts.text: Common swifts stay airborne up to 10 months at a stretch. Eating, sleeping, mating, all of it in the air.
comments: The only thing that brings them down is breeding. Everything else in their life happens without landing.
Send this to whoever complains about a six hour flight: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/sky-high-sleepers/

posts.text: Rosy boas are the one snake where the standard humidity advice will actively hurt them.
comments: Care sheets for tropical boas warn about humidity running too low. This is a desert species, and excess moisture is the primary trigger for respiratory infection here.
Scale rot runs on the same root cause. Damp or dirty substrate, discolored belly scales, sometimes an odor. Both fix the same way, keep the aspen genuinely dry.
Full guide on the reversal and the rest of the list here → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/rosy-boa-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: A pistol shrimp's claw snaps fast enough to make a bubble that briefly hits the temperature of the sun's surface. The bubble does the killing, not the claw.
comments: The snap alone stuns or kills prey outright. It never has to make contact.
Grab this for the next person who says small means harmless: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/finger-snapping-shrimp/

posts.text: Cuttlefish do not just camouflage. They hypnotize. Patterns ripple across the skin fast enough to freeze a crab in place.
comments: The freeze only has to last long enough for the strike. That is the whole point of the light show.
Send this to whoever thinks color change is only about hiding: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/hypnotic-skin/

posts.text: Mice are hardy for their size until they suddenly are not, and the thing that gets them is usually already established before you see it.
comments: Most serious mouse respiratory disease is Mycoplasma pulmonis, the same pathogen behind chronic respiratory disease in rats. It can sit asymptomatic a long time before it flares.
Sneezing, nasal or eye discharge, noisy or labored breathing, a hunched posture, ruffled coat. Damp, drafts, dust, and poor ventilation all raise the risk.
Full guide on the humidity range and the rest of the list here → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/mouse-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Magpies were the first non-mammal to pass the mirror test. Dot on the feathers, shown a reflection, and they go straight for the dot.
comments: A cleaner wrasse has since joined them, which is its own strange thing to sit with. A fish, on the same list.
Grab this for the next person who calls a bird brainless: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/magpie-self-awareness/

posts.text: Fireflies are not glowing, exactly. They are running a chemical reaction on a compound called luciferin.
comments: Which makes every summer field you have ever watched a slow chemistry demonstration you did not know you were attending.
Send this to whoever you used to catch these with: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/glimmer-in-the-dark/

posts.text: Parrotlets come with a full-size parrot personality in a body small enough that problems move fast.
comments: Avian vets treat respiratory signs as a same-day emergency until proven otherwise. Full guide on what to watch for → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/parrotlet-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Sperm whale clicks reach 230 decibels. Loudest sound any animal makes, and you can feel it in your chest from meters away.
comments: It is not for show either. That is how they find giant squid thousands of feet down in total darkness.
Grab this for the next person who thinks the deep ocean is quiet: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-loudest-animal-alive/

posts.text: Cheetahs purr constantly, even on the exhale. The tradeoff is that they cannot roar at all.
comments: They are the only large cat that does it, which puts them closer to a house cat than to a lion on this one specific thing.
Send this to whoever assumed every big cat roars: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/cant-stop-purring/

posts.text: Cherry shrimp rarely die of disease. They die of a molt that went wrong, and by then there is nothing you can do.
comments: An adult sheds every 3 to 4 weeks. A failed one shows as a complete white band around the middle of the body instead of a clean split at the head.
It usually traces to a swing in general hardness, an oversized water change, a calcium poor diet, or water too cold to support the molt. Stable GH and gradual changes are the actual fix.
Full guide on GH targets and the rest here → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/cherry-shrimp-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Owls do not have eyeballs. They have fixed tubes locked into the skull, which is why the head has to do all the moving.
comments: Up to 270 degrees of rotation, purely as compensation for eyes that cannot move at all in their sockets.
Grab this for whoever thinks the head spin is a party trick: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/tube-eyed-head-rotators/

posts.text: Reindeer eyes change color with the season. Gold in summer, blue in winter.
comments: The blue shift is a night vision upgrade for Arctic twilight. They are the only mammals known to do it.
Send this to whoever thinks they already know everything about reindeer: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/blue-eyed-arctic-shifters/

posts.text: Discus are not actually delicate. They just give you a much narrower margin for error than other fish do.
comments: Ich treatment here goes to roughly 90F rather than the usual 82 to 86F, because discus already live warm and have less headroom left. Full guide → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/discus-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: A threatened hagfish dumps up to a liter of slime in 0.1 seconds. It expands in water and clogs the predator's gills completely.
comments: The predator is the one with the problem at that point. The hagfish just leaves.
Grab this for whoever thinks fish have no defenses: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/instant-slime-escape-artist/

posts.text: Peregrine falcons dive over 240 mph. Nothing else on the planet moves that fast under its own power.
comments: Tiny bony baffles in the nostrils are what make it survivable, they keep the air pressure from wrecking the lungs at that speed.
Send this to whoever wants to argue about the fastest animal: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/fastest-animal-alive/

posts.text: Jackson's chameleons get recommended as the friendlier step up from a veiled. Same failure mode ends most of them.
comments: Metabolic bone disease, from inadequate calcium, D3, or UVB, and early cases respond far better than advanced ones. Full guide → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/jacksons-chameleon-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Naked mole rats are nearly immune to cancer and can go 18 minutes without oxygen by running their metabolism on fructose, like a plant.
comments: They are also one of the only mammals that cannot regulate their own body temperature, which is a strange thing to trade for near cancer immunity.
Send this to whoever thinks evolution optimizes for looks: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/cancer-proof-and-cold-blooded/

posts.text: Tuataras have a light-sensing third eye on top of the skull and a lineage older than the dinosaurs.
comments: Their metabolism is slow enough to push them past 100 years, and they are the last survivor of an entire reptile order. Not a lizard, despite looking like one.
Grab this for whoever lumps all reptiles together: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-reptile-with-a-third-eye/

posts.text: Lovebirds hide illness so well that noticing usually means it is already further along than it would be in another pet.
comments: They are particularly susceptible to PBFD, which is often fatal, has no cure, and is highly contagious, so testing a new bird before introducing it is real prevention. Full guide → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/lovebird-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Bats are the only mammals that actually fly, not glide. Some fire off 200 calls a second and read the echoes into a live map.
comments: That map is built in total darkness, updating continuously, purely from sound bouncing back. Nothing else in the mammal world comes close.
Send this to whoever still calls them flying mice: https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/built-in-sonar/
